function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points (2024)** | Topic | Summary | Practical Tips | |-------|---------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits: 35–55 mph on rural roads, 45–65 mph on highways, 25–35 mph in residential zones.
• “No speed limit” zones exist on some rural roads; drivers must use “reasonable and prudent” speed. | • Always obey posted signs; use a GPS that updates speed limits. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• The law applies to all vehicles, including motorcycles (helmet required). | • Check the seat‑belt reminder light; it turns on if a belt isn’t fastened. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | • Use voice‑activated commands or a mounted hands‑free system. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education programs, possible jail time. | • Designate a sober driver or use rideshare services. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks.
• “Yield” signs require slowing and yielding to traffic or pedestrians. | • Always check for pedestrians before proceeding through intersections. | | **School Bus** | • Stop on both sides of the road when a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children.
• The bus’s stop sign and flashing lights must be observed. | • Do not pass a stopped school bus until the lights stop flashing and the stop sign is retracted. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle is turning left. | • Use mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are allowed only when visibility is less than 200 ft. | • Keep headlights clean; replace bulbs promptly. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker.
• Towing a vehicle requires a proper tow bar and a towing permit if the vehicle is not registered. | • Keep registration documents in the glove compartment. | | **Parking** | • No parking on sidewalks, crosswalks, or within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid handicap placard. | • Use designated parking lots whenever possible. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Texas uses speed cameras in certain counties; fines are issued automatically. | • Drive within posted limits to avoid automated tickets. | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens. | • Pull over to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle passes. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | • Keep proof of insurance in the vehicle. | ### Quick Reference for Common Violations | Violation | Typical Fine | Possible Penalties | |-----------|--------------|--------------------| | Speeding (up to 10 mph over limit) | $100–$200 | Points on license | | Speeding (over 10 mph) | $200–$500 | Points, possible license suspension | | Seat‑belt non‑compliance | $100–$200 | Points | | Cell‑phone use while driving | $200–$400 | Points, possible license suspension | | DUI (BAC 0.08–0.15) | $500–$1,000 | License suspension, mandatory education, possible jail | | DUI (BAC > 0.15) | $1,000–$2,000 | License suspension, mandatory education, possible jail | ### Resources - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – [https://www.txdmv.gov](https://www.txdmv.gov) - **Texas Transportation Code** – searchable online at the Texas Legislature website. - **Local County Courts** – for specific traffic ticket information and court dates. Feel free to ask if you need details on a particular law, how to contest a ticket, or anything else!
